speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, could you tell me when the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension first started? Also, are you experiencing any vomiting or changes in bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Is the distension accompanied by visible peristaltic waves, and has the baby passed any stool or gas recently? 
I will also request an abdominal X-ray to check for signs of obstruction or Hirschsprung's disease. 
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The delayed passage of meconium and radiological findings strongly suggest Hirschsprung disease. I need to confirm the presence of aganglionosis, so I will request a rectal suction biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the biopsy is normal, we must rule out other causes of functional obstruction. Has the baby had any episodes of bilious vomiting, and can you describe the consistency and frequency of the stools he does pass?
